findings.title: getBaseConditions() can return an un-parenthesized OR expression
findings.body: `getBaseConditions()` returns the raw SQL fragment as-is when there are no filters, and for `org`/`team` scope that fragment is `(A AND B) OR (C AND D)` with no surrounding parentheses (see the reducers at lines 171-174 and 204-207). Any caller that composes it, e.g. `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "startTime" > $x`, gets `(A AND B) OR ((C AND D) AND "startTime" > $x)` because `AND` binds tighter than `OR`. The first OR branch then bypasses the extra predicate entirely, which silently returns rows that should have been filtered out (a correctness and potential data-exposure problem, since the OR branches are the authorization clauses). The fragment returned by `getBaseConditions()` (and by `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()`, which are public) should always be wrapped in parentheses, e.g. `return Prisma.sql`(${conditions})``.

findings.title: Public findMany() removed without updating consumers
findings.body: The public method `findMany(findManyArgs: Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs)` is deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a SQL fragment and performs no query. Any existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` (tRPC insights routers, etc.) will fail to compile/run, and no such callers are updated in this PR (only the service and its test are touched). Either keep a `findMany`-equivalent that executes the query using the new SQL conditions, or update all call sites in the same change.

findings.title: Constructor options type widened, losing discriminated-union safety
findings.body: The constructor parameter type was changed from the discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` to the new flat `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` (`scope: "user" | "org" | "team"`, `teamId?: number`). With this signature, `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` (no `teamId`) type-checks, then fails `safeParse`, sets `this.options = null`, and silently yields `1=0` — i.e. insights pages render empty data instead of surfacing a compile-time or runtime error. Keep the discriminated union as the public input type, or throw when validation fails so misuse is visible.

findings.title: Unreachable branches in getBaseConditions
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always resolves to a `Prisma.Sql` instance (never null/undefined — it returns `NOTHING_CONDITION` on failure), so `authConditions` is always truthy and the `else if (filterConditions)` / final `else { return NOTHING_CONDITION; }` branches at lines 76-80 can never execute. This dead code hides the fact that the "no authorization" case is already represented by `1=0`; it should be simplified to avoid future readers assuming a null-auth path exists.

findings.title: SQL expectations depend on unordered DB row order
findings.body: The org-scope and team-scope assertions compare the generated `Prisma.Sql` (including its bound `values`) against literal arrays such as `[testData.user.id, user2.id, user3.id]` and `[testData.org.id, testData.team.id, team2.id, team3.id]`. Those arrays come from `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds` / `TeamRepository.findAllByParentId`, which are issued without an `ORDER BY`, so Postgres may return rows in any order and the test will fail intermittently. Sort the actual/expected ID arrays before comparing, or assert on membership rather than exact array ordering.

findings.title: Caching tests deleted without replacement
findings.body: The `describe("Caching")` block covering `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` memoization was removed entirely. The caching behaviour still exists in the service (lines 84-95 of insightsBooking.ts) and is now untested, so a regression (e.g. the `=== undefined` check for the nullable filter cache) would go unnoticed. The tests could have been ported to the new `Prisma.sql` expectations like the others.
